pieces.caption: Some things stay in the house, whoever knocks. Mark a note secure and Rotli moves it to wiki/_secure/ and keeps it away from remote models and web lookups; the Librarian leaves it alone. Rotli also recognizes common secret shapes (API keys, private keys, card and identity numbers) and treats them the same way. rotli.co

pieces.about: Study 01 · Motion Résumé: a motion designer's reel for a fictional studio, one accent on a dark ground, 60 fps with motion blur.
Study 01 · Motion Résumé, designed for vertical: the same reel re-stacked, each section named in the serif.
Study 02 · Vertical App Ad: floating UI and word-by-word serif captions for a fictional scheduling app, made for Reels and Shorts.
Study 02 · Vertical App Ad, designed for landscape: the UI on the left, the captions on the right.
Study 03 · One-Shape Loop: one shape becomes every state of a booking, on springs, seamless at 60 fps.
Study 03 · One-Shape Loop, designed for landscape: the state named on the left, a state indicator on the right.
Study 04 · Print Carousel: three rules for calmer meetings in four slides, risograph overprint, halftones and grain, composed so X's four-image grid keeps each rule and its picture.
pieces.caption: Three rules for calmer meetings, printed in two inks. A study drawn in code for a fictional product, Oriel.

pieces.about: Study 04 · Print Carousel, re-composed for square: the picture beside the words, every slide centred for X's four-image grid.
pieces.caption: Three rules for calmer meetings, printed in two inks. A study drawn in code for a fictional product, Oriel.

pieces.about: Study 05 · Sketch Explainer: a blueprint that draws itself on and works out a meeting time from three calendars.
Study 05 · Sketch Explainer, designed for vertical: the week runs top to bottom, the people across the top.

pieces.title: Behind the Film
pieces.about: Four slides: how the 60-second film was drawn in code, from the brief and the agent to the goldens and the soundtrack, and where all of it is open.
pieces.caption: How we drew Rotli's 60-second film in code, in 4 slides. Every frame is a function: a brief, a prompt, Claude Opus 5.5 on the open-source anidoodle engine, hashes that catch a changed pixel, and a soundtrack written sample by sample. All of it is open: studio.rotli.co

pieces.about: Study 06 · Kinetic Poster: type only, full bleed on signal orange, outline-to-fill words, marquee rows and colour-flash cards.
Study 06 · Kinetic Poster, designed for vertical: one word per line, taller marquee rows.
Study 07 · Particle Word: dust becomes a word, a point-cloud sphere with orbit rings, a wave, and one bright point.
Study 07 · Particle Word, designed for square: the word on two lines.
Study 08 · Data Story: a dark dashboard whose widgets animate their own data, numbers rolling like odometers.
Study 08 · Data Story, designed for vertical: one column, the headline figure on top.
Study 09 · Shape Morph: one shape becomes every primitive over a reactive dot grid, seamless at 60 fps.
Study 09 · Shape Morph, designed for landscape: the shape's name on the left, a step indicator on the right.
Study 10 · Layer Stack: isometric slabs stack into a product over a sunburst, a node map and a memory starburst, with serif caption ladders.
Study 10 · Layer Stack, designed for square: the stack centred, captions above it.
Study 11 · Pixel Parable: an 8-bit office parable, an icon swarm and a pixel serpent, with crisp UI cut-ins.
Study 11 · Pixel Parable, designed for landscape: the office widens so the team and the manager share one frame.
Study 12 · Mascot Track: a robot mascot and one metaphor, build the track, then race the road to the checkpoint.
Study 12 · Mascot Track, designed for square: the mascot larger, captions above, a tighter road.
Study 13 · Annotated UI: hand-drawn circles, arrows and highlights mark up a live invite, then the fix rebuilds it.
Study 13 · Annotated UI, designed for landscape: the invite on the left, annotations and captions on the right.
Study 14 · Numbered Steps: giant numerals morph from step to step, each with its own scene, ending on a comment call to action.
Study 14 · Numbered Steps, designed for square: the numeral left, the words right.
Study 15 · Paper Collage: torn kraft paper, paper hands and stop-motion timing press the missing piece into the week.
Study 15 · Paper Collage, designed for landscape: the calendar stays left while the computer, portraits and captions change on the right.
Study 16 · Agent Network: four agents pass packets along dotted edges, a conflict resolves in orbit, and a handoff log prints every hop.
Study 16 · Agent Network, designed for vertical: the network in the upper two thirds, the log panel below.
Study 17 · Dot Matrix: one fixed grid of dots becomes lettering, a filling month, a clock and a ring, only by growing and changing colour.
Study 17 · Dot Matrix, designed for vertical: a taller grid, the month in two blocks, lettering on two lines.
Study 18 · Feed Storm: a notification feed floods to 47, a cursor sweeps it down to three, and they fold into one decision.
Study 18 · Feed Storm, designed for landscape: the feed on the left third, the decision card and captions on the right.
Study 19 · Offer Cards: plan cards fan, compare and flip, ending on a comment call to action.
Study 19 · Offer Cards, designed for portrait (4:5): the cards side by side, the setup fee as an equation.
Study 20 · Before / After: one week in two states behind a sweeping divider, crowded and warm on one side, calm on the other.
Study 20 · Before / After, designed for landscape: the divider is vertical, captions in side columns.
Study 21 · Morph Launch: a product launch in one continuous take, caption to glass prompt to dot to mark to app window, read with depth of field, at 60 fps.
Study 21 · Morph Launch, designed for vertical: two-line captions, a phone-width window, the tiles in one column.
